title: LRU Cache

content.problemStatement:
You're given a fixed `capacity` and a space-delimited sequence of `ops` to
run against an initially empty Least Recently Used (LRU) cache. Each token
is one of:

- `"put_<key>_<value>"` - insert or update the value for `key`, marking it most recently used, evicting the least recently used entry first if this exceeds capacity
- `"get_<key>"` - return the value for `key` if present, marking it most recently used, or `-1` if absent

**Simulate the operations in order and return a list containing the result of every "get" operation, in the order they occurred.**

Accessing a key with either `get` or `put` always counts as using it.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.input: capacity = 2, ops = "put_1_1 put_2_2 get_1 put_3_3 get_2 put_4_4 get_1 get_3 get_4"
sampleTestCases.explanation: get_1 returns 1 and makes 1 most recent; put_3_3 evicts 2 (least recently used); put_4_4 evicts 1

sampleTestCases.input: capacity = 1, ops = "put_1_1 get_1 put_2_2 get_1 get_2"
sampleTestCases.explanation: with capacity 1, put_2_2 immediately evicts the only entry, key 1

sampleTestCases.input: capacity = 2, ops = "put_1_1 put_2_2 put_1_10 get_1 get_2"
sampleTestCases.explanation: put_1_10 updates the existing key 1 to value 10 and marks it most recently used, it does not count as a new insert

hints: Using a dummy head node can simplify edge cases when modifying the head of the list.
Fast and slow pointers (Floyd's cycle-finding algorithm) can help detect cycles or find the middle element in a single pass.
Always update next pointers carefully to avoid creating accidental cycles or losing references to the rest of the list.
